newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NZ investor Graeme Hart buys Burns Philp stake.
newsitem.headline: NZ investor Graeme Hart buys Burns Philp stake.

text.p: Burns Philp & Co Ltd said on Monday that New Zealand investor Graeme Hart had become a substantial shareholder, buying about 14.9 percent of the troubled yeast and spice group.
The stake was purchased through Hart's private company known as the Rank Group.
Burns Philp managing director Ian Clack said the company welcomed Hart's presence on its share register, and his "demonstration of confidence" in its long term strategy.

The announcement, which was made after the share market had closed, ended speculation about the identity of a mystery buyer who snared the stake in the company last last week, paying the top price of A$2.50 a share through broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
At this price, the troubled company was valued at A$1.33 billion (US$994.5 million).
The price paid by Hart surprised traders and other brokers as it was well above the company's recent trading range and 47 cents above Burns Philp's closing price on Thursday, June 12.
Clack said Hart's presence on its share register would contribute to the stability of the company, which recently announced it intended to sell its herbs and spices business.

"Mr Hart has a demonstrable track record in enhancing the value of companies with which he has been associated and we welcome the contribution he will be able to make as a major investor in Burns Philp," Clack said in a statement.
Speculation on the identity of the buyer had centred on a private individual, given that Burns Philp is engaged in ongoing litigation over the Estate Mortgage Trusts.
Estate Mortgage, for which a Burns Philp subsidiary was trustee, collapsed in 1990 with A$600 million in losses.
Hart had been seen as a likely buyer following the sale last year of his New Zealand publisher and book retailer Whitcoulls to U.S.-based Office Products for NZ$320 million.

Hart's Rank Group confirmed in a statement that it held 14.9 percent of Burns Philp and, subject to Foreign Investment Review Board approval, was entitled to a further 1.3 percent under an option agreement.
Rank said it intended to be a long-term investor and had met with Clack in Sydney on Monday.
"The meeting was constructive and covered a range off issues including Burns Philp's current objectives with which the Rank Group identifies," it said.
Burns Philp shares closed down 3.8 cents at A$2.392.
